extracted.intended_audience: Research teams (Coordinating PI + co-PIs) applying for the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative Collaborative Science Awards in neurodegeneration
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and selection criteria for submitting Letters of Intent and Full Proposals to the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative Collaborative Science Awards (three-year, $350K/year) aimed at small interdisciplinary teams studying foundational mechanisms of neurodegeneration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget amount and duration (fixed)
rubrics_metrics.description: $350,000 per year for 3 years ($1,050,000 total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget is a fixed amount: $350,000 total costs per year for three years. Application budgets must reflect the actual costs of the proposed project. Budget is one page maximum. Indirect costs are limited to up to 15% of direct costs and are included within the $350,000 annual budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs cap
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs are limited to up to 15% of direct costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect costs must be included within the $350,000 annual budget (i.e., cannot be added on top).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant degree and position eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold a PhD, MD or equivalent degree and have an academic appointment in an independent faculty position or equivalent at an accredited institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be in an independent faculty position or equivalent at an accredited college, university, medical school, or other research facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be submitted by domestic and foreign non-profit organizations, public and private institutions, such as colleges, universities, hospitals, laboratories, units of state and local government; and eligible agencies of the federal government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants are made to institutions on behalf of named award recipients; the Coordinating PI's institution will receive funds and distribute to other members' institutions. Note: foreign institutions may not subcontract to US institutions—be mindful when selecting the Coordinating PI/institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration size and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborations should include two to four Principal Investigators (minimum of two and maximum of four).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least one member of the collaboration should be a physician with active clinical engagement in an area relevant to the proposal. One PI should be designated as the Coordinating PI to manage the group and be the administrative contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinating PI institutional requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Coordinating PI must be affiliated with the institution submitting the application and grant funds will be awarded to that institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Coordinating PI takes responsibility for managing the collaboration and for administrative contact with CZI and any grant partners (including Silicon Valley Community Foundation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Physician/clinical engagement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one member of the collaboration should be a physician with active clinical engagement in an area relevant to the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement emphasizes alignment with clinical context even though the RFA is for foundational/basic mechanistic work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of research (foundational, not translational)
rubrics_metrics.description: This RFA is explicitly not a translational or clinical development RFA and rather is aimed at foundational and mechanistic studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful projects should be grounded in human biology and disease pathology and aim to provide rigorous foundations for future translational/clinical work. The scope should focus on foundational science (as opposed to translation and clinical application), aligned with clinical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific focus examples / scope guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: common disease mechanisms across diseases; probing mechanisms in human cells/tissues/models; non-neuronal influences; improved animal models; cell population susceptibility; causal hypotheses for core cellular mechanisms; disease progression and aging studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CZI encourages projects that are underexplored or address gaps in well-developed mechanisms; proposals should be grounded in human biology when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to contribute to community tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators will be asked to contribute to the development, validation and dissemination of robust, reliable, and scalable experimental and analytical tools for the broader neurodegeneration community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CZI will provide infrastructure support for community tool development and dissemination. Examples include validated platforms for human cell biology, scalable cellular analysis tools, robust shared animal models, unique human tissue resources/protocols, benchmark datasets, and computational/machine learning approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open science and data/publication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: CZI supports a consent, sharing, and publication policy for open and rapid dissemination of research results, including methods, data and reagents, and a policy for software development that maximizes accessibility, reuse, and shared development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications related to funded work must be submitted to a preprint server (e.g., bioRxiv) before first journal submission. Experimental protocols should be made publicly available (e.g., protocols.io). All software should be made available under maximally permissive open source licenses where possible. Exceptions will be considered where impossible or counterproductive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: All datasets either curated or generated through the project should be made publicly available and easily accessible online, when feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include metadata, documentation, and intended computational use cases as appropriate. CZI will work with researchers to identify routes and best practices; controlled access is acceptable where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reagent and resource sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources and reagents developed with this funding support should be available for rapid dissemination to the community, where possible in an accessible community repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Addgene for plasmids/DNA reagents/viruses, Jackson Labs for model system lines. Applies to cell lines, transgenic organisms, plasmids/clones, antibodies, and other reagents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human tissue consent policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All human tissues should be fully consented to permit full sharing of the resulting data and any resulting tools, in accordance with laws and regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any desired exceptions to this policy must be identified at the time of application and may affect the application's chance of success. Investigators are encouraged to discuss challenging consent situations with CZI scientific staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical conduct standards
rubrics_metrics.description: CZI advocates the highest standards for the ethical conduct of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to requirements of their own countries, grantees should adopt procedures for the use of animals, for the ethical treatment of human subjects and tissue donors, and for obtaining written informed consent. CZI regards NIH policies as a strong model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process: two-stage (LOI then Full Proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial Letter of Intent (LOI) followed by invited Full Proposal; LOIs due April 3, 2018; invited full proposals due June 21, 2018; finalists interviewed Sept 10-13, 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters of Intent will be evaluated and finalists invited to submit full proposals. Finalists will be interviewed in person; applicants must hold Sept 10-13, 2018 for potential travel. All submissions must go through apply.chanzuckerberg.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: LOI required components and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: LOI includes Applicant Details, Organization Details for Coordinating PI, Project Details, Collaboration/Project Description, References, Biosketches, Letters of commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific LOI word/page limits: Project Summary (100 words max); Description of each PI's role (400 words max); Collaboration/Project Description (1000 words max) split into Scientific goals and Tools/resources; Biosketches five pages max (NIH format or similar); references have no word/page limit; letters of commitment signed from each co-PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal components and strict formatting/word limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Full proposal upload as single PDF containing Abstract, Proposal Body, Figures (optional), References; plus Budget, Updated Biosketches, Institutional Approval Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract/Project Summary 250 words max; Proposal Body 2000 words max and must include Scientific goals and Tools/resources sections; Figures limited to one page inclusive of legends; References no page/word limit; Budget one page max; Updated biosketches five pages max (NIH format or similar); Institutional Approval Form required. The formatting and component requirements, including word and page limits, will be enforced by the review team; materials exceeding limits or not following requirements will not be considered during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional sign-off requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must have administrative sign-off at the time of submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that do not have administrative sign-off at the time of submission will not be reviewed. Coordinate submission with appropriate officials according to institutional policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria (what awardees will be judged on)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of awardees will be based on: the quality of the proposal, expertise, and capacity of the collaborative group; interest and potential impact of the questions for understanding mechanisms of neurodegenerative disease; degree to which the proposed work brings new ideas and opens up new lines of investigation; potential of the collaboration partners to contribute to and benefit from a highly collaborative interdisciplinary Network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should address fundamental mechanisms rather than translational strategies, but with a clear clinical context. There is emphasis on high risk/high impact and novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process and final decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: CZI will evaluate applications for scientific merit, seek independent expert review, invite finalists for interviews, and make final decisions by CZI staff in consultation with scientific advisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no expectation of any specific number of awards; CZI reserves the right not to recommend funding. CZI does not provide feedback on decisions for unfunded proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: All submitted applications will be kept confidential to the greatest extent possible, except as necessary for evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the grant award, funded proposals will be shared across the Challenge Network; unfunded proposals will remain confidential. Application materials will not be returned to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting, deliverables, and participation obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: For awarded projects, financial statements and progress reports will be due at the conclusion of each grant year; investigators must participate in regular investigator meetings, including annual investigator meetings in the Bay Area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific deliverable requirements will be outlined in the award notification. Costs of travel to meetings and other Network travel should be allocated from Award funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other funding, carryover, and no-cost extension policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees may obtain funds from other sources provided there is no conflict with meeting terms of the CZI award. Unused research funds may be carried over to the following year and requests for no-cost extensions will be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure any additional funding does not conflict with award terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: IP and software licensing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: CZI does not retain rights other than a use right to data, published results, and intellectual property that result from the research; CZI supports policies that enable broad reach and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All software should be made available through maximally permissive open source licenses. In some cases commercialization (patents) may be appropriate, but intellectual property should be made freely available for academic and non-commercial use and generally subject to non-exclusive commercial licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility exclusions and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for the Collaborative Science Award may not apply for the Ben Barres Early Career Acceleration Award; proposals including activities in OFAC-sanctioned countries are not eligible; Facebook employees (including subsidiary employees) are not permitted to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CZI reserves the right to decide if an applicant and applicant organization meet eligibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged applicant profiles (priorities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are strongly encouraged from investigators new to the field of neurodegeneration, from those with interdisciplinary training and experience, and from women and underrepresented minorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators working in relevant fields outside neurodegeneration (cell biology, immunology, metabolism, physiology, computational biology) are encouraged if they can make a strong case for relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview attendance requirement (logistics constraint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalists invited for interviews must be available to attend in-person interviews in the Bay Area (Sept 10-13, 2018).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If travel to the Bay Area is not feasible, contact sciencegrants@chanzuckerberg.com to discuss. Finalists will be notified in early August and are requested to hold those dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission portal requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must be completed and submitted through the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative’s online grants management portal at https://apply.chanzuckerberg.com/
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is recommended that applicants familiarize themselves with this portal well in advance of deadlines.
